R.Foley · 32:07
Ray Foley, as course record holder with 10:45, arrived as the race started and the 'A's already chosen, so he also went into the 'B' quartet.

Sure we were still 6th but Ray Foley was right on the back of the pack, just 2 seconds behind 5th. AFD were looking fairly certain of 2nd but both the first two teams were fielding non-Surrey runners and Thames were believed to have turned out a second-claimer, so that County title was within reach.

Team Captain 'Gerry' Adams found himself pushed into 2nd place by the Priory's Ellis-Smith and then Ray Foley briefly regained the lead on the third stage only for international Jon Solly of Herne Hill Harriers to storm past with an aggressive 12 mins. 59 secs.

Now Gerry likes a fast start while Ray Foley prefers to come through as the race progresses, so it was a surprise when the runners poured out of the woods at the end of lap one and it was Ray heading our Captain as they slithered across the muddy playing fields in the bunch chasing Ranelagh's Dave Benton.

Both Ray Foley and Gerry Adams went into the race below par and poor Gerry suffered badly as the distance covered increased. It was only the attentions of Mike Webb, delighted to be in the scoring six, that kept him going at the end.
(b) Ray Foley, becoming one of the cornerstones of our teams on road and country – "right on the back of the pack". (c) The opening Reebok Surrey League lineup at Brockwell Park.

Clive was holding up well as our fourth scorer, Ray Foley was setting himself up for a high position and … what was this … eighteen year-old Kevin Quinn, fresh from a fine run in the Surrey Schools was our 6th man.

The race was intended to be held over 5k but the runners did an extra lap in error. 9 Wimbledon 10k: 7, R.Foley 32:02; 10, M.Kazimierski 33:20; R.Bale 39:24. Team: 1, Belgrave 105; 2, Ranelagh 194; 3, Collingwood 255.

And then it came together: Clive Gilby (took him longer to get there than he thought it would), Lee Hurst (with Carly having travelled from Manchester to Euston, to Waterloo, to Wimbledon), Ray Foley (with Anna and new baby Tess), Phil Carstairs (would he ever let us down) and others all arrived within a few minutes.
This year, with Jim Estall and Ray Foley running so well and with Kevin Nash expected to take part we thought we had a really good start in the men's event.
